But we are told that hundreds of years later, the Israelites had lost the purpose and understanding that this picture served. In **2 Kings 4** Hezekiah became king and had to right many of the wrongs in the land;

*He removed the high places, and brake the images, and cut down the groves, and brake in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made: for unto those days the children of Israel did burn incense to it: and he called it Nehushtan.*

The picture of the spiritual became a physical idol. The Heavenly lesson became bonds of the carnal.

This is where the Pharisees, Sadducees and scribes are at in the time of Christ. They have lost sight of the spiritual application for these things, and worship the symbol instead.

And so the carnal ordinances were to them an idol. And the work of their flesh in keeping these things replaced their faith in the Lord. They became self-righteous. They used the keeping of these ordinances as how one becomes righteous, rather than faith in what it represents, the Christ to come. And so, they become holier than thou  hypocrites. And later, Judaizers seeking to impose their vain traditions on the newly born again Gentiles. Circumcision, sacrifices, and the keeping of holy days such as the sabbath.

teachings.title: The judgments of God are ever relevant
teachings.summary: Only the ceremonial law was done away in Christ, so Christians should learn the moral judgments of Exodus, which will be enforced in the Millennium where the saints judge.
teachings.text:
Exodus 21 begins the judgments of God that flow from the implications of accepting the covenant with the children of Israel, the 10 Commandments.

*The law of the LORD is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple. The statutes of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the LORD is pure, enlightening the eyes.*

These statutes given through Moses, the moral law, is part of the covenant of being God's people. The right judgments that make His people holy, even today. None of the moral law was done away with in Christ. Only the ceremonial law, the ordinances and Levitical duties and sacrifices.

**Hebrews 9**
*8 The Holy Ghost this signifying, that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing:*

*9 Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience;*

*10 Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.*

*11 But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building;*

*12 Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.*

But His moral law is eternal, and these judgments set as the rules that will be enforced with a rod of iron in the Millennium. We should consider each, and understand the intent behind them all calls back to administration of the 9 commandments that remain following the fulfilment of the Sabbath.

Saved Christians have an obligation to know and understand these judgments and the spirit of their purpose, that we may serve as judges in the Millennial Kingdom.

*But his delight is in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night.*

There's a tendency to gloss over these things as "archaic" or not relevant, but they are ever relevant and key to understanding many of the commands given in the New Testament.

They also are fairly straightforward and need little interpretation. Over the next couple days I will post the chapters pertaining to the law and we can discuss them in chat. There's some misunderstanding and common questions people have, that I can help with, but again it's not very difficult textually.

teachings.title: The dietary laws a living parable of holiness
teachings.summary: The clean and unclean food laws were a schoolmaster teaching holiness, done away in Christ, so we are holy by the heart and not by what we eat.
teachings.text:
The dietary laws of the Levitical priesthood were part of a series of ordinances and rites of cleanliness that served as a way *to make a difference between the unclean and the clean.* To provide this distinction as a lesson to the people, the law being a schoolmaster, that they may better understand the holiness of God.

*Ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.*

As Peter writes in his first epistle, declaring the priesthood of the believer, *Because it is written, Be ye holy; for I am holy.*

It is an example. A means of separation that the Lord instituted with Moses and Aaron to demonstrate this concept. A living parable.

But as Christ Jesus says, it's not what goes into our mouth that is unclean, but the spirit by which it is received, and what proceeds out of our own mouth. And we know that out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.

The Isralites were given a chance to commune in assembly with God. To see their faith in His salvation be practiced before them with the ceremonial washings and sacrifices. To witness the spiritual through the physical, that they may come to understand God, and in it, Christ.

Now the time of reformation had come, the death and resurrection of Christ, and these carnal ordinances and diverse washings and sacrifices and oblations were done away with.

**Hebrews 7:11-12**
*If therefore perfection were by the Levitical priesthood, (for under it the people received the law,) what further need was there that another priest should rise after the order of Melchisedec, and not be called after the order of Aaron? For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law.*

And as Peter has revealed to him by God, that the "unclean," the people who were not a people, the Gentiles, were now to be folded into the promise of the kingdom, of the "clean."

*What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.*

And so now, graft in, we are called to be holy for He is holy. Not by the food we eat. Not by the things that enter into the mouth, by what's in our hearts and what we profess.

teachings.title: Love thy neighbour came from Leviticus
teachings.theme: Love thy neighbour in the law
teachings.summary: The laws against lying, talebearing and partiality flesh out love of neighbour, a commandment from the same God who forbade sexual immorality, not something Jesus invented.
teachings.text:
*Ye shall not steal, neither deal falsely, neither lie one to another. And ye shall not swear by my name falsely, neither shalt thou profane the name of thy God: I am the Lord.*

*Thou shalt not go up and down as a talebearer among thy people: neither shalt thou stand against the blood of thy neighbour; I am the Lord.*

These items flesh out the commandment against bearing false witness, both in rumor and backbiting and in matters before the law. Swearing falsely, profaning the Lord, taking His name in vain. Note it is tied in with stealing, and defrauding people, lying to one another.

Not robbing a man of his wages, but paying what is due as it is due. Not using false weights and measures. Not judging unrighteously, not being a respecter of persons, favoring the rich over the lowly. Not doing favors for a protected class, or for buddies, but dealing squarely.

Cursing the dead (who cannot hear you) or placing a stumbling block before the blind who cannot see, being dishonest in treachery and cruelty.

Do not hate your brother in your heart. This doesn't mean you can't be righteous in anger for a trespass, but it does mean you cannot hold that grudge after reconciliation or redemption is paid. But we are to rebuke our neighbor who is in sin, or who trespasses against us, that they may come to forgivnessand peace with you. Not out of anger or wrath, but love.

Which brings us to the second of the great commandments as Jesus preached; Love thy neighbor as thyself. On this, and on loving God, hangs the whole of the law.

Many modernists believe that Jesus invented this commandment, and that it is in variance with the Old Testament, "more wrathful God." That Jesus "taught love, not division, maaaaan." But they err not knowing scripture.

Those who seek to say that the prohibition against sexual immorality in chapter 18, for example, are done away with by the two great commandments of the NT, ignore that those commandments come from the same exact God in the same exact place in scripture.

teachings.title: All things are good for meat
teachings.summary: Jesus and Paul show dietary laws are vain carnal ordinances, yet the greater good is to love the weaker brother and not give him occasion to stumble.
teachings.text:
Dietary laws amended to the sanctification process of the believer often end in the place where "Pharisees were offended" having made those carnal ordinances into works of righteousness themselves.

Jesus declares the vanity of these carnal ordinances and dietary laws. Paul reminds that in Jesus all things are good for meat (meat means food to eat in the Bible, not just flesh of animals). But the greater good is loving your brothers and not tempting them to betray what they see as separation and sanctification. To not offend their conscience to please yours. To not be spiteful to those weaker in the faith. To not give them occasion to stumble in their walk.

teachings.title: The Jerusalem council and the Judaizers
teachings.summary: Acts 15 rejects the Judaizers' circumcision and law-keeping for salvation, while the letter's precepts on idols, fornication and blood were for sanctification, not salvation.
teachings.text:
In Acts 15 we see the early Christians in the independent churches of Asia Minor were being led astray by Judaizing heretics, trying to bring those saved by grace through faith back under the yoke of law, and through the rite of circumcision. That they were trying to mix grace with works, with "repenting of sin" through obedience to the law, including the carnal ordinances and dietary laws of Moses, and by physical circumcision, which could be considered like unto baby baptism, or any other of the so-called sacraments false churches add to the Gospel as a requirement.

We see Paul and Barnabas return to Jerusalem an an assembly of Apostles and the appointed elders, deacons of the church there at Jerusalem. Some believing Pharisees, retaining a bit of their holier than thou ways, have joined in demanding Gentiles circumcise.

 Peter speaking against the judaizers, reminds them that they as Jews could not attain perfection through the law, only by believing in the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ shall any be saved.

God through His word continues to hammer home that the only salvation is through faith, delivered through God's grace, in the name of Jesus. Not of works of the law. Not of what we do.

James, who takes charge of the assembly (not 'Pope Peter'), gives scripture to answer to the issue. This is what we should all do when faced with a question regarding anything. Search the scriptures and see what God has to say.

James recommends and the others agree, to instead write edifying epistles to the churches, to tell them that these judaizers are wrong, that the law is past, but to remind and encourage them that they should continue to avoid idols, the meat sacrificed to them by their country men, fornication, and consumption of blood, (all of which we see in later epistles, being instructed to the churches), that *they may do well.* These are given as percepts for behavior and sanctification, not as requirements for salvation, given to avoid confusion, especially with those Gentiles who had been in synagogue prior to believing on Christ, and were familiar with the law of Moses. They attempt to head off future contentions by indicating that these things still should be avoided.

Now idolatry and fornication had been of old, God's law. Before Moses. And the restrictions on blood and strangulation, from Noah. These were not done away with in Christ the way the temple sacrifice, diverse washings, circumcision and the levitical priesthood were, and we will see this explained in the Epistles of Paul in greater detail.

The Apostles send these letters and emissaries, Judas and Silas with Paul and Barnabas to visit these churches and add weight to the doctrine being preached.

The chapter ends after some time has past, and the pair of evangelists reflect on making a trip to visit the various churches they'd helped plant among the Gentiles, and we see the falling out they had regarding Mark, who had previously been taken with them on their missionary journey, and we are told he had bailed at Pamphylia when it got tough. Paul doesn't want him along, Barnabas does and the long time friends in Christ part ways.

We see that even those of one accord in the faith don't always see eye to eye, and differences of opinion and strife strike even the best men of God.

teachings.title: Abraham's seed is Christ, and believers are heirs
teachings.summary: Believing Gentiles are Abraham's children through Christ the one seed, the law was a schoolmaster and not a separate dispensation, and no Jew, Rome or church can annul or add to God's covenant of faith.
teachings.text:
Paul asks the supposedly saved Christians of Galatia, *Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? He therefore that ministereth to you the Spirit, and worketh miracles among you, doeth he it by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?* The answer is obvious to those that have the Spirit inside them, testifying to its truth. But to those still believing on their own righteousness to redeem them, this question is vexing indeed.

Quoting scripture regarding Abraham, who the Bible says in **Genesis 15:6** *And he believed in the Lord; and he counted it to him for righteousness.* This proof of our faith in God's promise of Christ Jesus being what is counted for righteousness is also quoted by Paul in **Romans 4** and in **James 2** (although to much consternation to those trusting their works to save them).

Paul reminds the Galatians that just because Jews come to tell them they need to add works of the law to their faith for salvation, that they hold no special place. That the Gentiles who received the same faith as Abraham are sons of Abraham, that all nations are blessed by Abraham's seed, that is Christ. Not seeds, plural, as in Jews after the flesh.

This chapter is also one of many nails in the coffin of dispensationalism, that wicked and often damnable heresy that places Jews in a higher regard than those that believe on Christ. The lie that they had a different way to be justified. Paul calls what they claim as a blessing, a curse.

The law was a school master, bringing those who lived under it to the understanding that no man can be justified by the works of the law. To remind them to keep the faith in the promise of God, rather than themselves. It was designed to bring them to faith, not a separate dispensation.

And of that covenant of faith, and the good news of it, no man may disannul or add to it. Read that part carefully. Understand what it means.

God made a contract with us. It is the promise of being made heirs to the Kingdom and the blessings that go along with being heirs. Being His sons. That promise only requires believing on Him to deliver on it.

Those who say they can take away your role in the promised kingdom, or adding requirements to receive it, who seek to annul or add to the covenant of God given in his testament, are liars. They can't.

Jews, Catholic church, the daughters of it, etc...cannot take away your salvation or add obedience to their traditions to receive the inheritance of faith given to Abraham, and promised by God to whosever believe. It isn't possible. They have no authority to change a covenant, a contract, given by God.

Paul says the law given to the Hebrews through Moses by God Himself didn't have the power to disannul the covenant He made with Abraham. Imagine having the hubris to think some institution of man could!

The law wasn't given to give life, but to condemn so we could understand we needed righteousness by faith.

Scripture says that God made a promise to Abraham, that faith in that promise justifies, that justification by the law is only possible by obeying the whole of it, that this is impossible, that if we place our faith in our ability to do the whole of the law, we becomes slaves to it, and that we all fall short, making the law a curse. But that in grace, we are saved by faith in Christ. Summarized:

*But the scripture hath concluded all under sin, that the promise by faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe.*

And if we believe?

.*.ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus.*
*For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.*
*There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. And if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.*

teachings.title: Bodily exercise profiteth little
teachings.summary: Every creature is good to eat being sanctified by the word and prayer, and godliness, not the flesh, is what profits, since God is the Saviour of all men, specially of those that believe.
teachings.text:
Now to edify Timothy in his role as evangelist to the Ephesians, Paul gives yet more advice as to the doctrines he should be certain to instruct the churches.

That every creature is good to eat, *For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer*, just as God told Adam and again to Noah. The dietary laws and carnal ordinances given to Moses for a season, done away with in Christ. This understanding will help the men of the church "be a good minister of Jesus Christ," not because of the food they eat, but rather the understanding of prayer and God's blessing. That, as Jesus said, *the flesh profits nothing,* rather they will *be  nourished up in the words of faith and of good doctrine.*

And so, avoid old wives tales, similarly, Jewish fables, and be about exercising godliness, their spirit, not the flesh.

*For bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come.*

We the saved, *having*, present tense, the promise of the life that now is and the eternal life that awaits, must exercise and grow, spiritually. Godliness is our gainz, for our eternal life will be built upon that, not our PRs at the gym.

*This is a faithful saying and worthy of all acceptation.*

And therefore, because of this doctrine of faith, living Godly, in the spiritual rather than the flesh, the *faithful sayings* Paul writes unto Timothy, he warns they will both labor to teach others, and be rebuked by those of this world, *because we trust in the living God, who is the Saviour of all men, specially of those that believe.*

(Note to calvinists, God is the savior of all men, specially those who believe. Christ died for everyone, especially to those who believe and are saved)

teachings.title: The sabbath was made for man
teachings.summary: Jesus taught that the sabbath pictured rest in Him and that what defiles is the heart, not outward ritual, a higher standard than the Pharisees' outward show.
teachings.text:
The chapter ends with two more challenges by the scribes and Pharisees to Jesus and His correction of their error.

First, they accuse Jesus and His disciples of not being pious enough to fast, and use the austere ministry of John the Baptist and his followers fasting to lend more credence to their own self-righteous fasting. To build a stronger "got ya" against Christ. And once again, Christ answers them with unassailable doctrine. How can they fast in the presence of the bridegroom? They celebrate while He is with them, and will fast once He's gone.

Jesus says one doesn't patch an old garment with new cloth, or place new wine in old skins, as a parable to what would happen. The cloth would rend from the inflexibility of the new cloth. The wine, fresh juice would ferment and tear the old skins. So to, He is saying He isn't there to "patch" the old failed ways of the Pharisees, to mend the old law. He's there to fulfill it and make it new again.

Mark shifts to another instance of the so-called holy men challenging Christ and the behavior of His disciples, as they glean corn in a field to eat on a sabbath. Jesus uses the example of David and his men when they were fleeing his enemies, eating the shew bread of the temple, despite that being reserved for the preists. That the sabbath was made for men, not men to the sabbath.

The Sabbath was designed to picture the rest we have in Jesus after salvation. It was meant to give rest to the weary. To teach as a schoolmaster the truth of Christ to the Hebrews. It wasn't meant to be a way of showing super righteousness by how closely you followed the tradition of man that sprung up around it. As a pups exercise to be seen of others.

That the rest we have in Jesus is the same. It's not our actions that sully us, but the context and spirit by which we commit them.

*All things are lawful for me, but all things are not expedient: all things are lawful for me, but all things edify not.*

It is similar to the story in **Matthew 15** where the Pharisees again question Jesus and His disciples, when they don't wash their hands in the ritual way before eating.

*Do not ye yet understand, that whatsoever entereth in at the mouth goeth into the belly, and is cast out into the draught?*

*But those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man. For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, blasphemies:These are the things which defile a man: but to eat with unwashen hands defileth not a man.*

A common teaching of Christ is emphasis on the spirit and heart by which we sin, the same as the spirit and heart of how we have faith. That it is the thought of wrath that is murder, thought of lust that is adultery. What our intent and what is in our hearts that God judges when we are His.

This is a higher standard than the Pharisees' outward displays of righteousness, while inwards they are ravenous wolves, full of sin.

However it cuts both ways, where in the trappings of what man sees as outward signs of sin may well be just their idea of what righteous looks like. Who put appearance over substance. Who sin in their hearts, polishing the outside of the cup, but defile themselves inwardly by their hearts.

As Jesus said to these hypocrites “*Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess."*

 It is perspective we should all keep in mind.

teachings.title: Onan's Sin Was Denying Seed to His Brother
teachings.summary: Onan was slain not for the act itself but for refusing to raise seed to his dead brother as God's law required, a passage commonly misread.
teachings.text:
Today on Judah Springer....

Judah, the son of Israel who had led his brothers to sell Joseph to bondage, is not a good guy. One of the reasons the brothers hated the young brother Joseph was that he brought an evil report back to their father, and we see from this synopsis of Judah's life, there was plenty of evil to report.

Judah falls in with a rough crowd of heathens, being best friends with an Adullamite. He marries a Canaanite woman and bears sons wicked enough to be slain by the Lord. The eldest, Er, isn't detailed what all he did, but it was wicked enough to get God's attention.

And when his wife was left childless by his death, Judah does try to do what is right by her and give her a child by his son Onan. This custom mirrors the law given by God to Moses.

**Deuteronomy 25:5**
*If brethren dwell together, and one of them die, and have no child, the wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger: her husband's brother shall go in unto her, and take her to him to wife, and perform the duty of an husband's brother unto her.*

This is the law and what's right in the eyes of God.

Of course, we see in the Gospels that the Sadducees use this to tempt Jesus;

**Matthew 22**
*23 The same day came to him the Sadducees, which say that there is no resurrection, and asked him,*

*24 Saying, Master, Moses said, If a man die, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.*

*25 Now there were with us seven brethren: and the first, when he had married a wife, deceased, and, having no issue, left his wife unto his brother:*

*26 Likewise the second also, and the third, unto the seventh.*

*27 And last of all the woman died also.*

*28 Therefore in the resurrection whose wife shall she be of the seven? for they all had her.*

*29 Jesus answered and said unto them, Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God.*

*30 For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven.*

*31 But as touching the resurrection of the dead, have ye not read that which was spoken unto you by God, saying,*

*32 I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.*

*33 And when the multitude heard this, they were astonished at his doctrine.*

It is in this context we see Judah offering Onan unto his daughter-in-law Tamar. But Onan refuses to give a son to his dead brother, knowing Tamar but spilling his seed on the ground. For this wicked act, God slays Onan as well.

Many think Onan's sin was pulling out, in general. That's not the case, it was the specific act of denying seed to his dead brothers wife, breaking the law and dishonoring everyone involved.

*And Onan knew that the seed should not be his; and it came to pass, when he went in unto his brother's wife, that he spilled it on the ground, lest that he should give seed to his brother.*
*And the thing which he did displeased the Lord: wherefore he slew him also*.

This misunderstanding of the scriptures has led to the term Onanism to describe a sin of not completing in a woman, and is often associated with masturbation.

The more you know.

teachings.title: A Priest After the Order of Melchisedec
teachings.summary: Christ is a High Priest after the order of Melchisedec, greater than Levi, and the change of priesthood disannulled the law of Moses.
teachings.text:
And so, having established Jesus Christ's nature and purpose and the order of things pertaining to salvation of grace, including the rejection of the Gospel of truth, Paul returns again to his thesis, directed at the believing Hebrews, that Jesus is our High Priest, after the order of Melchisedec. Different than the order of Aaron. Separate from those Levite-born.

By necessity of a better testament and through the eternal life of Jesus, who was sinless and without spot, both the priest and the sacrifice, He is our High priest promised in the Psalms.

Paul is building the case that they who were under the law but now are saved by faith in Christ have no need of the human preists given by Moses, and the sacrifices and carnal ordinances are done away with in Jesus.

Some call this replacement theology, the replacement of the Jews as the "chosen people of God," with the Holy nation created from all tongues and kindreds by those who believe. But, as we see by Abram's tithing to Melchizedek, the High Priest of the most high God. Melchizedek who blessed Abram, *and without all contradiction the less is blessed of the better.*

The Levites are of Abraham. And in Abraham, paid tithes to the King of Peace. The ruler of Salem. The High Priest of God who is without beginning or end. Like unto the Son of God. The less paid honor to the greater.

This is an important concept for the early church, which had many raised as Jews. Paul is laying out the replacement. The disannulling of the law of Moses. *For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law.*

He reasons that the Levitical preists were made such without any oath by God, but the Spirit through David made such an oath regarding Jesus, that He be made a High Priest after the order of Melchisedek. Another promise made by God who cannot lie. To whom we have our full trust in, and see Jesus as the surety of the promise of eternal life, and so we must accept His vows given through His word. And the implications thereof are clear;

*But this man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood. Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them. For such an high priest became us, who is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens; Who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people's: for this he did once, when he offered up himself. For the law maketh men high priests which have infirmity; but the word of the oath, which was since the law, maketh the Son, who is consecrated for evermore.*

Amen!

teachings.title: I Regarded Them Not
teachings.summary: Hebrews 8:9 shows the Jews broke the covenant and God regarded them not, so salvation was never by bloodline but always by faith.
teachings.text:
The entire New Testament is a case against dispensationalism and the idea that Jews are still "chosen," and exempt from the faith of Christ unto forgiveness that is the New Testament, the *better* covenant. But Hebrews 8:9 is one of many silver bullets, putting down the heretical idea that Jews today are special:

*Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.*

God's covenants, His promises to a nation, like all covenants, carry if-then statements that if not fulfilled, exempt the parties from its terms. The Lord says here in no uncertain terms that the Jews continued not in His covenant AND I REGARDED THEM NOT.

It can't be any plainer. Just as John the Baptist says to the Pharisees, *Think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.*

It was never about genetics or bloodlines, except so far as the promise of Christ, which wasn't to the Jews but to all men. The root and the seed.

And salvation from Hell and death was always by faith, calling upon the name of the Lord. But the law that served to convict those who transgressed, a schoolmaster, is replaced by the law in man's heart, and the knowledge of the truth in Christ Jesus.

The Old Testament then, which some still believed they were under as Paul wrote this, was ready to vanish away.

teachings.title: Judaizers and Rome Rebuild the Veil
teachings.summary: Hebrews refutes the Judaizers, and today Zionism, Hebrew roots and Rome likewise put priests and ordinances between man and God, though Christ is the only High Priest.
teachings.text:
God's message to the Hebrews, explaining the need for the end of the Mosaic law, the Levitical priesthood and the carnal ordinances comes to give these 1st century Hebrews confidence to reject the call to return to the vain traditions of man that many Jews were pushing early believers towards. The Judaizers who we see in Acts and the epistles persecuting and infiltrating the churches of the time seeking to return Christians to bondage under the law. Circumcision was a large part of it, but there were those claiming that they needed priests, sacrifice at the temple, to keep the days and feasts. The diverse washings. The vain traditions of man that became the Pharisaical laws.

But repeatedly, again and again, the Bible shows us this being reproved. That this was replaced in Christ and the liberty which was purchased by His blood upon the mercy seat in Heaven. Not a temple made by hands but that spiritual tabernacle in Heaven.

And even so, today, there are Judaizers among us, creeping in unawares. Bringing things like Zionism, "Hebrew roots," and other heresies to bring the believer back under the yoke of the law.

Further, we have established cults from the whore of Babylon in Rome and its harlot daughters, that seek to mend the veil and rebuild the earthly tabernacle, made by their own evil hands. To separate man from God again through their own preists, carnal ordinances, feasts and days. Bloodless redemption though human mediators. Grace doled out by weekly sacrifices. Dead works as a means of satisfying transgressions of the law which they yoke their followers with.

They *compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves.*

They say "call us father," "Papa." Padre. Pope.
When Jesus said "*call no man your father upon the earth: for one is your Father, which is in heaven."*

They place themselves between God and man to prevent the will of the Father, and the offer of the free gift of salvation, eternal life given by grace through faith.

But the letter to the Hebrews, from God through the Spirit, promises us that we have A, singular, High Priest after the order of Melchisedek, that in Christ Jesus we are forgiven our sins, adopted into the inheritance, and free to boldly go before the throne of God, directly to the Father, in the name of the Son. The Son Who isn't ashamed to call us brethren. Amen!

This is the better testament. This is the good news. Let no man prevent you. Now is the hour of salvation. Be born again unto eternal life. Repent from dead works to serve the living God.

teachings.title: A Fearful Thing to Fall into God's Hands
teachings.summary: Those who taste the truth and turn back to the old covenant have no sacrifice left for sins, only a fearful expectation of judgment.
teachings.text:
So if that is the practical application of our faith, and the understanding of our salvation in Christ, the end of sacrifices for sin, boldly going before God, serving Him and assembling together, then what is the implication for those who instead turn aside the faith and the new covenant to return to the yoke of the old?

*For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.*

*He that despised Moses' law died without mercy under two or three witnesses: Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?For we know him that hath said, Vengeance belongeth unto me, I will recompense, saith the Lord. And again, The Lord shall judge his people.*

*It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.*

Again, this is a warning to those who may have tasted the truth but are withdrawing themselves, influenced by the Judaizers who were afflicting believers with the doctrine of dead works.

That if there is no reconciliation by animal sacrifice, if there never has been, and you have this knowledge of the truth in Christ but turn away back to the Old Testament, rejecting the New, you remain under the wrath of God. You have the guilt and fear of judgment upon you. Worse, the knowledge of the truth adds to that burden of guilt, how much worse God's vengeance is on those who should know better? And by the end of this epistle there can be no doubt. If they fall away from faith in Christ and refuse to repent towards God after hearing this preached, well, it's a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

teachings.title: Is this the fast that I have chosen
teachings.summary: In Isaiah 58 God condemns self-afflicting fasts done for strife and show, and says the fast He chose is to loose bands of wickedness and do works of mercy, the sabbath being rest that pictures Christ.
teachings.text:
This chapter of Isaiah is incredibly relevant here. The opening verse, one of the most famous lines used by preachers for millennia. The LORD tells the prophet Isaiah, preaching in the Spirit to cry aloud, to tell His people, the house of Jacob of their inequities. To reprove them of their sins.

 God, anticipating the protests of the people who may resist the idea that they are guilty before Him, says yet they seek Me daily and delight in my ways, they do the ordinances of the law, the works. The sacrifices and the offerings and the dietary laws and carnal ordinances. They delight in doing these things.

They may say, Didn't we fast? Lord didn't you notice? We afflicted ourselves, and you didn't see? Didn't we fast on your day, Lord?

And God answers this rhetorical question for us; He doesn't regard their fasting and self affliction, because they are doing it for themselves selfishly, while they are openly oppressing others. It's not a spiritual act of humility, but arrogant and prideful.

God says to them that they fast for strife and debate. To hold it over others. To judge the righteousness of others. To hold the people bound to a yoke of works-based self-righteousness, not the liberty found in faith.

God asks, is this a fast I have chosen? Did He order them to do these acts of penance on the Sabbath? Is it part of the ordinances given in the Old Testament, the covenant in effect at this time? He asks incredulously, "*a day for a man to afflict his soul? is it to bow down his head as a bulrush, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under him? wilt thou call this a fast, and an acceptable day to the Lord?*"

Basically God is saying, is that what the Sabbath was made for? To afflict yourselves with fasting and ashes and sackcloth? To burden the people? Is this what you call an acceptable day to the Lord?

God continues to berate them, again asking rhetorically, "Isnt the fast I chose to loose the bands of wickedness? To undo the heavy burdens? To let the oppressed go free? "*And that ye break every yoke?*"

The Sabbath was to be a day of rest, that pictured the rest found in Christ. A day without labor, that people could understand that God did all the work so that they could share in His rest. A picture of salvation. Not to bind people to doctrines of devils, abstaining and fasting and weeping and wailing in sackcloth, covered in ashes.

God is like I never told you to do any of this. It is sin.

God continues, saying He gave us the Sabbath that we may do things that a workday prohibits getting done. Feeding the poor, going out and finding them that you may give them shelter in your home. To see the naked and give them clothes. To do the works of charity and mercy that we are called to do as His people. Not self flagellation and misery. Not heaping these carnal ordinances and requirements on to the people who are meant to be free to do His will.

He promises if they do those things he actually asks of them, He will bless them and their light will shine, the glory of God our reward. The multitudes of blessings that would come upon them span the next several verses.

But these false acts of piety aren't it, chief.

God tells us, directly, in no uncertain terms, exactly what His stance on all these made up fasts and acts of communal suffering in His name is. It is inequity and sin. Doctrines of devils.

And God promises us directly, the benefits of doing His will in this, and not our own:

 *If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the Lord, honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words: Then shalt thou delight thyself in the Lord; and I will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father: for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it.*

teachings.title: God's if/then covenants with nations
teachings.summary: God's covenants with nations are conditional, judging nations by their works while He judges individuals by faith, and a nation that turns from wickedness can still be healed.
teachings.text:
We see near the end, after the triumphant singing and dancing unto the Lord, that the Isralites first begin to complain. And God makes a covenant with them as a nation, through Moses.

 *If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of the Lord thy God, and wilt do that which is right in his sight, and wilt give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of these diseases upon thee, which I have brought upon the Egyptians: for I am the Lord that healeth thee.*

All of God's covenants with the Hebrew are if/then. All come with responsibility of the people to hold to what God asks. This is the covenants with nations. With the people on this earth. God judges us as individuals spiritually by faith, but God judges nations on earth by their works.

This invitation to nations is still around today. It is how a godly nation that turns from its wicked ways becomes spared the evil God will do unto it.

*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

teachings.title: If ye will obey, a peculiar treasure
teachings.summary: The Sinai covenant was conditional and Israel broke it, so it was replaced by the new covenant and those saved in Christ are now God's peculiar people, refuting dispensational Zionism.
teachings.text:
IF *ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine.*

This is the foundation of the covenant at Sinai, the promise made to the children of Israel by God, that IF they kept it, they would be a peculiar people, special to God.

God judges nations on earth by their works. He judges people as individuals by their faith. His promises to nations are conditional. They are if/then. To us as individual souls, the only condition to be His is faith in Christ.

The if/then covenant with Israel, that they broke themselves repeatedly, despite God's longsuffering and mercy, despite being given chance after chance to get right, they broke entirely with the Crucifixion, the rejection of Hia Son Jesus. But it is in Jesus that are made partakers of the new and better covenant. The better testament. And the old one is done away with.

*For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second.*

And where was the fault of the first? In the Israelites.

*For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord. For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people: And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest. For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more. In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away.*

This is the bookend to the Saini covenant, fulfilled:
*I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.*

And this should be the final nail in the coffin for the Dispensationalist Zionist heresy that God is still on the hook for the first covenant. No, He has replaced the physical nation with a new one. Israel was to be a peculiar people, but failed. Now His peculiar people are those saved in Christ.

*But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light; Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.*

teachings.title: The sabbath, a picture of rest in Christ
teachings.summary: The sabbath pictures resting in Christ's finished work, so salvation is by faith alone, and keeping the seventh-day sabbath to be saved, as Seventh-day Adventists do, is judaized bondage while Christians gather on the Lord's day.
teachings.text:
**Mark 2:28**
*Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.*

**Matthew 11:28-30**
*Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.*

Chapter 31 provides an additional teaching on the sabbath, God instructs Moses to tell the people they are not to work on the last day of the week, least they be cut off and put to death. That the sabbath is a day of rest to memorialize His perpetual covenant, that it is by faith in the Lord that sanctifies us.

It is a fitting picture of Christ, in whom we are called to rest on His perfect work for salvation. That salvation is by faith alone, not of works. And if you reach the end and are trusting in your works rather than the sabbath God provided, you're perishing. You will be cast out and put to death, which is Hell.

People struggling with the idea that our works do not save us don't understand how the Sabbath is a memorial for the covenant of Christ. That we are free of the yoke of the law in regards to righteousness, because by the blood of Christ God will not impute sin to those that are saved when we are called to the Kingdom. They miss the point of the 3 sabbaths in a row between Passover and Easter Sunday, the first day of the week. That no works of the law shall save us. Jesus did it all.

7th Day Adventists and others under the yoke of the law keep the old testament sabbath, the last day of the week, in order to be saved. It is judaized nonsense.

Christians celebrate and gather on the first day of the week, the Lord's day, in remembrance of His resurrection and the establishment of the new testament. As a memorial throughout our generations that we may know He is the Lord that sanctifies us.

**Galatians 5:1**
*Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.*

teachings.title: Restitution, not prisons: God's just law
teachings.summary: God's law of restitution for theft is just and perfect, and a nation living by His judgments would be better than man's criminal justice system.
teachings.text:
As we continue through the ordinances for the Levitical priesthood and sacrifices, we are also given more insight into the law, building on the fundamental of loving thy neighbor.

The sin of robbery by guile or by violence, by any dishonest means, was punished by restitution plus 5%, and a trespass offering. That's it.

Now as we saw yesterday, this required a confession of the wrong in order to share in the sacrifice for atonement, and obviously to restore the person who suffered loss.

God says this is just.

Man says we must create an entire criminal justice system with prisons and punishment, cops and robbers.

As we saw in Exodus 21, 22, there are more provisions for theft, and include instructions for those impenitent to or destitute to be given to servitude to repay. If they are caught breaking in and killed by the owner, there is no blood guilt. If there is harm done. Eye for an eye. Tooth for a tooth. Stripe for stripe.

God's law is perfect. It may not be able to save us, sinners as we all are. But for a nation to live by His perfect judgments, if they were to be followed, it would be a much better country. In our founding, much of the original laws came from the Old Testament. They are right and just.

**1 Timothy 1:8-11**
*But we know that the law is good, if a man use it lawfully; knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers, for whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind, for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine; according to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.*

teachings.title: Abstaining from meats: a sign of false religion
teachings.summary: Imposing meat bans or Levitical dietary laws, whether Catholic or Judaizing, is a doctrine of devils and a red flag of a cult.
teachings.text:
There are some false religions that impose carnal ordinances of abstaining from types of meats to be "holy," what the Bible calls "doctrines of devils."

This applies not only to the Catholic practices of not eating meat on Fridays, which we see is totally foolish and unbiblical, but more and more in Judaized Evangelical circles, the imposition of Levitical dietary laws.

But we who are saved in Christ know that nothing is unclean if it is eaten in thanksgiving, blessed by God.

This provides a simple test for the believer to see if they are involved in a cult or false religion. Any implementation of the Old Testament ordinances done away with in the reformation that is Christ, should be a giant red flag.

teachings.title: God's civil law still judges nations
teachings.summary: The civil punishments of Leviticus 20, unlike the ceremonial ordinances, are God's standard for judging nations and remain in effect today.
teachings.text:
**Leviticus 20** begins laying out specific punishments for the violations of the civil laws given to Moses and Aaron by God, especially the paganism and the sexual immorality listed in the previous chapters. The sins of those whose lands the children of Israel were entering into, and the land the Lord freed them from, Egypt.

And as God frequently has stated in giving this law, the purpose was to separate the people unto God and away from the error, whoredoms and abominations of the other nations. To be holy because He is holy.

The law of God is perfect. His judgments are righteous. A just nation seeking after the Lord, who have the fear of God, would implement these strictures and punishments, that their nation not be judged, and the land that the Lord has granted them the habitations thereof wouldn't spew them out.

And so, as a practical matter, these things given by God, not to be confused with the ordinances and sacrifices that were done away with in the reformation of Christ, but rather are His law by which He judges nations. They are in full effect, even today. And His wrath is clearly upon those nations that don't follow His precepts.

teachings.title: Cut off for Molech and familiar spirits
teachings.summary: God commanded that those who gave children to Molech or went after mediums be cut off, showing His perfect will for a people seeking to be holy.
teachings.text:
And so, practically, physically, these laws give us insight to the perfect will of God for a people.

We start with a continuation of the following after false gods from chapter 19, where if a man offers his seed, that is his children, to Moloch, the false god of the Canaanites, he shall be cut off. Not allowed to defile the house of the Lord. Stoned to death, God's face turned from him. Reprobation. He is rejected and it is up to the people to do as God commanded and not to ignore his presence among them. This rejection is both physical and spiritual,  (I want to focus on the literal application as we go through the list of sins and punishment, tying in the spiritual application afterwards.)

Next he warns against those who go after mediums; those who have "familiar spirits," and after wizards, they too shall be cut off, the mediums and wizards stoned to death. Note these things are closely aligned with the false gods, because they are not only satanic but mean the person has no respect for the Lord, no fear of the living God, and has no faith in Him that saves, but rather seeks another god of their own invention. Reprobate concerning the faith, and physically cut off from the nation seeking to be holy. Sanctified.

*Sanctify yourselves therefore, and be ye holy: for I am the Lord your God. And ye shall keep my statutes, and do them: I am the Lord which sanctify you.*

Again, separation by keeping God's statutes, that He may sanctify us. Something that Israel failed to do, and were cut off for when, after the longsuffering of God was over, Jesus had come in the flesh.

teachings.title: The temple and sacrifices could not save
teachings.summary: The temple and sacrifices were a gift to those already justified by faith, not the means of it, as Abraham was saved before circumcision.
teachings.text:
In this, God also wants those Jews who were going into the temple, to pay lip service to the ordinances and sacrifices, while not having the heart of a believer, that these acts cannot save them. No flesh is saved by works of the law. They were given as a means to understand the promised Christ. They were given after the promise that if they believed on the Lord, He'd be their God and they'd be His people.

Just as Abraham was saved by faith before circumcision. The blood of bulls and goats didn't save them.

And to remind them, God says he will destroy the temple that they are counting on to save them. Just as He previously destroyed Shiloh, the sight of the Tabernacle in the North, over run by Philistines and Assyrians, and laying in ruin during the days of Jeremiah.

The sacraments and the temple were a gift to those already justified by faith. Not the cause or means of that faith.

Faith cometh by hearing and hearing by the word of God. OT and NT.

And as we know, *God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets*...the word of God came upon those He sent. And the people did not harken unto them. None believe the report. And so, the judgment of God is just, being provoked to wrath by a stiff-necked and gainsaying people.

*Since the day that your fathers came forth out of the land of Egypt unto this day I have even sent unto you all my servants the prophets, daily rising up early and sending them: Yet they hearkened not unto me, nor inclined their ear, but hardened their neck: they did worse than their fathers.*

And so, God says the time is coming where the Temple itself and all the high places and altars to false gods they had set up, will be destroyed. Babylon is coming.

teachings.title: Make no peace with reprobates
teachings.summary: He teaches that the Canaanites were reprobate nations God commanded destroyed, and that believers today should mark and avoid known reprobates, keep them from their congregations and urge magistrates to execute God's law.
teachings.text:
*But thou shalt utterly destroy them; namely, the Hittites, and the Amorites, the Canaanites, and the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites; as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee: That they teach you not to do after all their abominations, which they have done unto their gods; so should ye sin against the Lord your God.*

Now, contrast the offer of peace we should make with the average men of this world, the unregenerate, or even the saved who have conflict with us, loving our enemies, showing mercy that we may make a brother of them... contrast that with how God commands the Israelites to deal with the nations of Canaan that have become abominations. Who are reprobates. The dogs. The swine. The idolators, passing their children through the fire. God proclaims that nothing that draws breath among them shall be spared. That the Hebrews should slay every last one of them, that they teach them not to do after their abominations. That they don't corrupt the people of God with their filth and unrighteousness.

Of course, today we do not have the power in this world to slay the reprobates among us. Our government has rescinded the laws against the sodomites, for example. It hardly even punishes the rapists and pedophiles among us. But this is instruction that we may take spiritually, and draw lessons from, even as we speak out to bring the magistrates back to executing God's law.

There are some people who are beyond saving. There are some people whom God has given up on. They have been given over to a reprobate mind, rejected of God. And to recognize them, God's word has given us multiple examples of how to know them, the primary one being their burning with lust one towards another, men with men, women with women. Who have left the natural use, to engage in unnatural lusts.

**Romans 1, Hebrews 6, 2 Peter 2, and Jude** provide us with warnings and what to look for. Jesus taught against the false teachers and against giving that which is holy to the dogs. Pearls before swine.

This is controversial today, but it is the whole word of God. We are to mark and avoid, as much as possible, those we can know are reprobate. Not in wrath. Not railing. But to cut them out of our lives as much as possible, and definitely out of our congregations.

**Romans 12:18** should be our default behavior when dealing with others;
*If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.* But we should never declare peace with reprobates, and invite them in, least they teach us, or our children, their abominations.

teachings.title: Nations judged for shedding innocent blood
teachings.summary: A nation that refuses to punish those who shed innocent blood, whether by repealing capital punishment, funding abortion or bombing innocents, is guilty of that blood and God will judge it, so believers must stand against it.
teachings.text:
**Deuteronomy 21** ramps up the commands of God in this, Moses giving of the law prior to entering the promised land. The land given as an inheritance to the children of Israel, if they maintain these rules to keep it. And right away God has let them know that the abominations of the Canaanites, their worship of idols and the shedding of innocent blood, were the cause of their own destruction. God judges nations for these things.

Here specifically, God gives provision for an unsolved murder along the wayside or in the wilderness. If a body be found, slain, and the elders of the nearest city do not know who did it, they were to take a heifer and offer a sacrifice, washing their hands of the matter. This of course is an image of Christ, as all the sacrifices pictured, the washing of the hands to show innocence before God for the bloodshed is just as Pontius Pilate did.

As the Lord declared to Noah; *Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man.*

**Proverbs 6:16-19**
*These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood, An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief, A false witness that speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren.*

**Psalms 11:5**
*The LORD trieth the righteous: but the wicked and him that loveth violence his soul hateth.*

When a nation has refused to slay those who shed innocent blood, they are guilty of it. And God will repay. Be it repealing capital punishment, refusing to sentence a murderer to death, justifying or even funding abortions, bombing Innocents abroad, all these things bring judgment on a people, and the land will spew them out.

**Leviticus 18:28**
*That the land spew not you out also, when ye defile it, as it spewed out the nations that were before you.*

God requires of us that we stand against the shedding of innocent blood and seek His justice against those that do it.

teachings.title: Reprobate silver: Jerusalem as dross
teachings.summary: Jerusalem broke the old covenant through idolatry, false prophets and oppressing the poor, despised God's longsuffering, and was judged and cast out like dross, which is why a new covenant was needed.
teachings.text:
We see here in the preaching against Jerusalem, where the Lord demands the prophet tell the Jews of their abominations and His judgment, that much of it mirrors those things given to Moses in the wilderness. The things God proclaimed should be dealt with by death. That the blood be upon the wicked and not on the people in the land.

But the children of Israel failed to uphold their end of the covenant and now faced the promised judgment.

**Hebrews 8:7-9**
*For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I Made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.*

The longsuffering of God, that nearly 1,000 years passed from Sinai and the law to the utter destruction of Jerusalem, was taken by the people to mean God wasn't present. That He no longer cared. That maybe He wasn't real.

His mercy and calls to repentance, ignored. The grace He offers men because of His love, taken advantage of. For greed and lust.

And false prophets preaching lies, saying "The Lord has spoken," when He hadn't. And devouring widow's houses and taking advantage of the poor and the fatherless.

**Matthew 23:13-15**
*But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in. Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation. Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves*.

The Lord looked for the righteous to be the salt that preserves, and found none. Just like in Sodom, where He told Moses if there were found just 10 righteous men, He would spare the cities. And so He promises to gather the wicked and melt them in flame like the molten metals they make their abominations with. For sacrifice in the mountains. For their idolatry, for their shedding of blood. For their degeneracy. Extortion, usury, greed.

They have become as dross. Impurities in the silver, cast out.

**Jeremiah 6:30**
*Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them.*

teachings.title: We have Abraham to our father
teachings.summary: The claim that the Jews inherit the land as Abraham's many children is the false basis of Zionism, since the promises were always conditional on obedience to God's covenant.
teachings.text:
**Ezekiel 33** concludes, the destruction of Jerusalem has happened. One who escaped comes to the prophet in the evening and tells him, but the hand of God keeps Ezekiel from responding until the morning came, and he was no longer struck dumb. And he receives the word of God.

The Lord says that those from the wastes and wilderness of Judah, who escaped out of the desolation of Jerusalem speak, saying that because Abraham was one, and was promised land, that they being many deserve the inheritance.

This is the argument made by Jews today. The basis of Zionism. The false doctrine that because they are children of the law, and many, the promise of the land given Abraham should apply even more so to them.

**Matthew 3:9**
*And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.*

The promises and inheritance was never given a people because of who they were. But by the condition of what they did. A condition repeatedly given.

**Exodus 19:5**
*Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine*

**Hebrews 8:7-9**
*For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.*

The word of the Lord upon Ezekiel stresses these same points. They are filled with violence and Idolatry and adultery and abominations.

For this, God says He will lay the land most desolate because of their abominations. Then they shall know He is the Lord.

teachings.title: Ezekiel's temple as what could have been
teachings.summary: Ezekiel's temple may be read as what could have been, since God with foreknowledge set conditional promises before Israel under the Mosaic covenant, which they failed to keep.
teachings.text:
Here in **Ezekiel 45**, the instructions for a temple and a time where there will be a priesthood of Zadok, Levites given land by cast lots for suburbs around the restored Temple. And sacrifices made for various offerings, the measure of which are given for "just balances," precise volumes, that nothing is cheated or anyone give more than another.

Similar to the existing Levitical laws, given unto Moses, the prophesied Temple in **Ezekiel 40-48** has similar Old Testament offerings and carnal ordinances, Sabbaths and holy days, done away with in the reformation of the New Testament.

We have looked at 4 main theories regarding this prophecy.; that it is symbolic and represents the church in Christ and Jesus our temple.

That it is literal, meant to be the design for the 2nd Temple Ezra will begin after captivity. That they fell short in grandeur and size.

That it is a future Temple, for the 3rd Temple leading up to the beginning of the Tribulation.

That it is a Temple in the millennial Kingdom, or in the eternal Kingdom.

All these theories have problems that make them more and more unlikely to be true. The secret things are His and we see through a glass darkly, but surely there's a purpose and a reason for Ezekiel to cap off his end times prophecies, that extend back to chapter 33. That the restoration promised also applies to the prophecy of the Temple.

Which brings us to another theory which I truthfully hadn't considered before. The interpretation of "what could have been."

First, we must acknowledge that God knows the end from the beginning, and the invisible things of what hasn't happened yet.

**Isaiah 46:9-10**
*Remember the former things of old: for I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me, Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure.*

God knows our decisions before we make them, but also allows us the free will to make them, and gives constant appeals to repentance, and encourages us to choose His ways and seek His paths.

The Lord gave the covenant to Israel through Moses with this clear understanding.

**Deuteronomy 30:15-20**
*See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil; In that I command thee this day to love the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply: and the Lord thy God shall bless thee in the land whither thou goest to possess it. But if thine heart turn away, so that thou wilt not hear, but shalt be drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve them; I denounce unto you this day, that ye shall surely perish, and that ye shall not prolong your days upon the land, whither thou passest over Jordan to go to possess it. I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live: That thou mayest love the Lord thy God, and that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life, and the length of thy days: that thou mayest dwell in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.*

God made these conditional promises to Israel as a nation, with the foreknowledge that they would fail. Unlike the Abrahamic and Davidic covenants, which were mostly unconditional (depending on the men themselves to believe God, and have it counted for righteousness), the Mosaic covenant, with the commandments and Levitical laws, depended on the people to keep up their end in order to obtain the Kingdom and the promises and the blessings that would come if they would. And in His grace, multiple opportunities for restitution if they failed.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

teachings.title: The promise was to Abraham's seed, which is Christ
teachings.summary: The promise to Abraham was made to his seed Christ and to all who are in Christ, the land promise was fulfilled under Joshua and kept conditionally under the Mosaic covenant, so Zionism wrongly gives the inheritance to unbelieving Jews.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 48** broadly captures the grandeur and love of God towards His holy land. This love is seen long before Israel as a nation enters in, or even exists. It was in the beginning, when God promised a land to Abraham.

**Genesis 12:1–3**
*Now the LORD had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, unto a land that I will shew thee: And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing: And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.*

The promise to Abraham was both for the land, and the Christ. Long before the exodus. Long before the wandering. Before Isaac was ever born, the land that would become Israel, the province of Judah, the city of Jerusalem, in the mountains of Zion, was set apart for God.

The blessings and inheritance made to Abraham, who believed God and it was counted for righteousness, was made to him and his seed. Jesus Christ.

**Galatians 3:16**
*Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.*

Zionism is a modern political ideology that takes the promise to Abraham, and rather than give the inheritance and blessing to Christ, and all who are in Christ, gives it to unbelieving, apostate Jews.

**Galatians 3:27–29**
*For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. And if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.*

The claim for the children of Israel to the land, by promise of God, was fulfilled in the time of Joshua.

**Joshua 21:43–45**
*And the LORD gave unto Israel all the land which he sware to give unto their fathers; and they possessed it, and dwelt therein. And the LORD gave them rest round about, according to all that he sware unto their fathers: and there stood not a man of all their enemies before them; the LORD delivered all their enemies into their hand. There failed not ought of any good thing which the LORD had spoken unto the house of Israel; all came to pass.*

The promise to Abraham was unconditional. But the promise made to Moses by God in the wilderness, for His people to occupy His land, was conditional.

**Deuteronomy 28:63–64**
*And it shall come to pass, that as the LORD rejoiced over you to do you good, and to multiply you; so the LORD will rejoice over you to destroy you, and to bring you to nought; and ye shall be plucked from off the land whither thou goest to possess it. And the LORD shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.*

Many Christians today will say "God keeps His promises! The Jews deserve this land!" They place political Zionism and the ethnic ultranationalism of the modern Jewish state as being part of an unconditional and irrevocable covenant with the people by heritage and genealogy.

But the Bible is clear, that the covenant made in the wilderness was explicitly conditional, that what was given to the people through Moses could not, by their failure, disannul the promise made to Abraham and his singular seed.

**Galatians 3:17–18**
*And this I say, that the covenant, that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot disannul, that it should make the promise of none effect. For if the inheritance be of the law, it is no more of promise: but God gave it to Abraham by promise.*

But the covenant made those 430 years after Abraham? It has faded away, replace by a better covenant with better promises, to all who are in Christ, regardless of their ethnicity or origin.

teachings.title: The inheritance belongs to all in Christ
teachings.summary: The land promise is fulfilled in the resurrection and the inheritance passes to all who have put on Christ, so Christians who give it away to modern Zionism for politics are like Esau selling his birthright.
teachings.text:
**Hebrews 8:7–10**
*For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord. For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people*

The promise to occupy the land will be fulfilled for the Old Testament believers, in the resurrection. The only "Zionism" that matters is Christ Jesus on His throne. The inheritance is passed to all who have put on Christ.

**Romans 8:14–17**
*For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God. For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father. The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together*.

This promise, the inheritance and blessings, is the heritage of all believers, from Adam and Abel, Seth and Noah, through every professing Christian today.

The spirit of Esau, who forsook his inheritance for a bowl of pottage, lives in Christians, who for political expediency seek to give it away.

**Hebrews 12:14–17**
*Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord: Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled; Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.*

This tearful repentance will be the case for many in the end times. Those who placed modern politics and bad theology above the joy unspeakable found in Jesus for all who believe, Jew or Gentile. Man or woman. Bond or free.
